enrichment.short_title: Secure tenancy succession after joint tenant's departure
key_facts: Westminster granted Mr Kazam and Mrs Hussain a joint secure tenancy of Flat 5, Brackley Court in 2005.
Mr Kazam left in 2011; Westminster amended internal records from joint to sole tenant while Mrs Hussain continued paying rent alone.
Mrs Hussain died in July 2020; her grandson Mr Rahimi claimed succession but Westminster terminated the tenancy as vesting in Mr Kazam.
HHJ Hellman found an implied surrender and regrant to Mrs Hussain alone; Lane J on appeal held there was none.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Tenant's appeal from Lane J's decision reversing the county court finding of surrender and regrant.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal dismissed (2:1); no surrender and regrant; grandson cannot succeed to secure tenancy.
enrichment.ratio: Where a joint secure tenancy continues, survivorship vests the tenancy in the absent joint tenant and succession is unavailable to a family member; implied surrender and regrant requires unequivocal conduct by landlord and all joint tenants, and Westminster's internal rent-account changes did not establish a new sole tenancy to Mrs Hussain.
legal_issues: Whether Westminster granted Mrs Hussain a new sole tenancy with Mr Kazam's consent
Whether internal records and rent payments amounted to surrender and regrant
Whether Mr Rahimi could succeed under Housing Act 1985 section 87

confidence.notes: Outcome, split decision, and core housing law analysis are explicit; judge metadata corrected.

enrichment.short_title: Part 5A deportation assessment for serious foreign offender
key_facts: Turkish national Mr Yalcin was sentenced to over five years for possessing a prohibited firearm.
The FTT allowed his human rights appeal, finding deportation disproportionate given impact on British children, especially D with special needs.
The UT set aside the FTT decision, holding it erred by failing to apply the unduly harsh test and by treating public-funds savings as countervailing public interest.
Andrews LJ granted permission only on whether the FTT erred in law.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal against Upper Tribunal decision setting aside FTT allowance of human rights claim resisting deportation.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal allowed; FTT deportation decision restored; UT erred on Part 5A assessment.
enrichment.ratio: For a foreign criminal sentenced to four years or more, tribunals need not expressly find 'unduly harsh' under Exception 2 before finding very compelling circumstances under section 117C(6); mischaracterising welfare/financial impact as a separate public interest rather than Article 8 interference is not necessarily fatal if immaterial to the balance.
legal_issues: Whether FTT had to apply unduly harsh test expressly before section 117C(6) assessment
Whether reference to public-funds savings redefined statutory public interest
Materiality of procedural shortcomings in FTT reasons

confidence.notes: Outcome and Part 5A analysis are central and explicit.

enrichment.short_title: Pit bull destruction order after CDO breach
key_facts: Kayleigh Dawson's pit bull terrier Lightning was subject to a contingent destruction order after being found to be a prohibited type.
On 7 February 2020 Lightning escaped and seriously attacked another dog and its handler while unmuzzled and off-lead.
Magistrates and the Crown Court ordered destruction under section 4B; Fordham J dismissed judicial review.
The owner argued the Crown Court applied too high a test and failed to consider CDO mitigation conditions.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal against Fordham J's dismissal of judicial review of Crown Court refusal to state a case and destruction order.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal dismissed; Lightning destruction order upheld.
enrichment.ratio: Section 4B requires the owner to prove on the balance of probabilities that the dog would not constitute a danger to public safety; the Crown Court correctly applied that test and was entitled to reject expert evidence; future CDO conditions cannot be relied on at the section 4B stage under the scheme in R (Golding) v Chief Constable of Kent.
legal_issues: Whether Crown Court applied an impermissibly strict test for prohibited-type dogs
Whether compliance breaches and escape were relevant to section 4B(2A) assessment
Whether future muzzling and lead conditions should be taken into account
linked_authorities: R (Golding) v Chief Constable of Kent
R (Grant) v Crown Court at Sheffield

enrichment.short_title: Patent sub-licence royalties on Zejula sales
key_facts: AstraZeneca sub-licensed PARP inhibitor patents to Tesaro for niraparib (Zejula) under agreements mirroring head licences with Sheffield and ICR.
Richards J held Tesaro must pay royalties on all Zejula cancer-treatment sales; Tesaro argued royalties applied only to patented uses.
The Compound definition linked licence scope and royalties to uses 'may be claimed or covered by' the Licensed Patents.
Tesaro contended only a minority of Zejula sales fell within the patent claims.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal against High Court interpretation of 2012 patent sub-licence royalty obligations.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal allowed; royalties only on patented uses not all Zejula sales.
enrichment.ratio: The italicised words in the Compound definition align the royalty obligation with the scope of the licensed patents, not all sales of niraparib as a cancer treatment; 'may be' connotes futurity and the Head Licences support co-extensive royalty and infringement scope; AZ's interpretation risked US patent misuse.
legal_issues: Meaning of 'the use of which may be claimed or covered by' the Licensed Patents
Whether royalty obligation extended to all Zejula sales for cancer treatment
Relevance of head licence wording and US patent misuse doctrine

enrichment.short_title: Deferring leave decision pending criminal investigation
key_facts: Chinese nationals applied for Tier 2 skilled worker leave in June 2021 while on immigration bail after overstaying.
The First Appellant was arrested in March 2021 on suspicion of money laundering; no charging decision had been made.
The Home Office deferred deciding the applications citing an outstanding prosecution, later citing complexity.
UT Judge Frances refused permission to judicial review; the Appellants later filed a fresh Article 8 application in August 2023.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal with permission of Males LJ against UT refusal of permission to bring judicial review of deferred leave decisions.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal dismissed; lawful to defer leave decision pending investigation.
enrichment.ratio: The Secretary of State has an implied power to defer deciding leave applications pending the outcome of a criminal investigation where the alleged conduct is potentially relevant to character and conduct under the Immigration Rules; delay awaiting a charging decision was not unlawful or irrational on these facts, and the August 2023 application rendered much of the challenge academic.
legal_issues: Whether SSHD lawfully deferred leave decisions pending criminal investigation
Whether delay became unreasonable or irrational
Whether Article 8 and section 55 duties were engaged
linked_authorities: R (New London College Ltd) v SSHD

enrichment.short_title: Part III financial remedies after Russian divorce
key_facts: Following a Russian divorce in March 2021, the husband applied under Part III for financial relief in England.
Sir Jonathan Cohen ordered a life interest in a €600,000 Greek property, €60,000 furnishings and about £60,000 pa maintenance for four years.
The husband failed to attend the final hearing and had extensive litigation misconduct with costs exceeding £9.5m.
The Court of Appeal increased housing to £1m and maintenance to £115,000 pa but dismissed other grounds.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal against Part III financial remedies order made in absentia after Russian divorce.
enrichment.outcome: Appeal allowed in part on housing quantum; other grounds dismissed.
enrichment.ratio: Where a Part III claim is needs-based and the judge lawfully proceeded in the husband's absence, the court will not revisit fact-finding; housing provision may be increased where the judge erred in limiting quantum to a Greek property rather than allowing London or Greece choice, and future dividends are a section 25 resource for maintenance assessment.
legal_issues: Whether trial in husband's absence was fair
Appropriate housing quantum and life interest structure under Radmacher
Treatment of litigation misconduct, costs orders and solicitor overspend
linked_authorities: Miller v Miller; McFarlane v McFarlane

confidence.notes: Detailed judgment with clear partial allowance; judge metadata corrected.

enrichment.short_title: County Court procedural failures quashed on appeal
key_facts: Koro brought a small claim against a car dealer for misrepresentation about a vehicle's condition.
A Deputy District Judge struck out the claim and ordered Koro to pay £5,000 costs without adequate reasons or fair hearing.
Koro appealed to a Circuit Judge who refused permission; permission to appeal to the CA was granted.
The Court of Appeal allowed the appeal and quashed the Deputy Judge's orders for procedural unfairness.
enrichment.procedural_posture: Appeal with permission against Circuit Judge's refusal of permission to appeal Deputy District Judge strike-out and costs order.
enrichment.outcome: Permission granted; appeal allowed; Deputy Judge quashed; procedural failures in County Court.
enrichment.ratio: Where a Deputy District Judge strikes out a small claim and makes a substantial costs order without giving reasons or allowing the litigant in person a fair opportunity to be heard, the decision is procedurally irregular and must be quashed; the Circuit Judge erred in refusing permission to appeal.
legal_issues: Whether strike-out and costs order were procedurally fair
Whether Deputy Judge gave adequate reasons
Whether Circuit Judge erred in refusing permission to appeal
linked_authorities: English v Emery Reimbold & Strick Ltd
Austin v Mayor and Burgesses of London Borough of Southwark

storyline.title: A car misrepresentation claim struck out without a fair hearing
storyline.summary: Koro sued a dealer over a faulty car, but a Deputy District Judge struck out his claim and ordered £5,000 costs without proper reasons. After permission was finally granted, the Court of Appeal quashed the orders for procedural failure.

stages.title: Small claim for misrepresentation issued
stages.what_happened: Koro issued a small claim against a car dealer alleging misrepresentation about vehicle condition.

stages.title: Hearing before Deputy District Judge
stages.what_happened: Koro appeared as litigant in person; the hearing proceeded without adequate opportunity to present his case.

stages.title: Claim struck out
stages.what_happened: The Deputy Judge struck out Koro's claim under CPR 3.4.

stages.title: £5,000 costs ordered against Koro
stages.what_happened: The Deputy Judge ordered Koro to pay £5,000 costs without adequate reasons.
stages.why_it_matters: Substantial costs for litigant in person.

stages.title: Circuit Judge refuses permission
stages.what_happened: The Circuit Judge refused permission to appeal the Deputy Judge's orders.

stages.title: Court of Appeal grants permission
stages.what_happened: Permission to appeal was granted given the procedural concerns.

stages.title: CA finds procedural irregularity
stages.what_happened: The court held the Deputy Judge failed to give reasons and denied a fair hearing.

stages.title: Circuit Judge erred refusing permission
stages.what_happened: The CA held the Circuit Judge should have granted permission to appeal.

stages.title: Appeal allowed; orders quashed
stages.what_happened: Stuart-Smith, Phillips and Baker LJJ allowed the appeal and quashed the Deputy Judge's strike-out and costs orders.
stages.why_it_matters: Claim restored to County Court list.

turning_points.label: Claim struck out
turning_points.impact: Ended claim without fair process.

turning_points.label: CA grants permission
turning_points.impact: Opened route to correction.

turning_points.label: Orders quashed
turning_points.impact: Restored claim for proper hearing.
